body:
A professional cleaning is more than a polish. It is the foundation of lasting oral health. At Valencia Dentistry, preventive care lowers your risk of cavities and gum disease and helps you avoid expensive restorative work later. This guide covers the clinical benefits, how cleanings save money over time, and a schedule based on your individual risk, so you can answer the question patients ask most: how often should I get my teeth cleaned?

## What a cleaning does for your health

- **Removes tartar and biofilm.** Brushing cannot remove hardened plaque (calculus). Ultrasonic and hand instruments clear the deposits that feed bacteria.
- **Prevents and controls gum disease.** Early gingivitis is reversible with professional care and better home hygiene. Regular cleanings reduce pocket depths and bleeding and slow progression to periodontitis.
- **Catches problems early.** Each visit includes an exam and periodontal screening that can reveal cavities, cracked teeth, oral lesions and signs of systemic disease sooner.
- **Protects restorations and implants.** Maintenance helps prevent decay under crowns and peri-implantitis around implants.
- **Improves breath and comfort.** Less bacterial build-up means less bad breath and less sensitivity from inflammation.

## How cleanings save money

Preventive visits are a small investment compared with restorative care:

- A cleaning and a filling cost far less than a root canal and crown for decay left untreated.
- Treating gum disease early, with scaling and root planing followed by maintenance, costs less than advanced periodontal surgery or replacing lost teeth with implants.
- Early detection avoids emergency visits, which tend to be more expensive and more disruptive.

Prevention also keeps your natural teeth, which is the best and most economical long-term solution. Dr. Nuriel Lavi's approach is conservative by design: extend the life of what you have and reduce cumulative cost.

## How often should you come?

The answer depends on your oral health, medical history and lifestyle. These are general guidelines; your schedule is set during your exam.

| Risk level | Who it covers | Suggested interval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low | Healthy gums, minimal tartar | Every 6 months |
| Moderate | History of cavities, heavier tartar, mild inflammation | Every 4 months |
| High or periodontal maintenance | Previous periodontitis, implants, smokers, diabetes | Every 2 to 3 months, or as advised after periodontal therapy |
| Children | Most children | Every 6 months, with fluoride and sealants based on cavity risk |

Factors that call for more frequent visits include heavy plaque, active gum disease, dry mouth, smoking, certain medications and conditions such as diabetes.

## What happens during a cleaning

1. **Exam and periodontal screening.** We check your gums for bleeding, measure pocket depths and look for anything suspicious.
2. **Scaling.** Ultrasonic and hand instruments remove plaque and tartar above and below the gumline.
3. **Polishing.** A prophy polish smooths the tooth surfaces and removes surface stain.
4. **Fluoride or desensitizing treatment**, when indicated, to strengthen enamel and reduce sensitivity.
5. **Home-care coaching.** Brushing, flossing and product recommendations to hold your gains between visits.

## Preparing for your visit, and afterward

- Brush and floss before your appointment.
- Tell us if you have sensitivity; topical agents can help.
- Mild sensitivity or gum tenderness for 24 to 48 hours after scaling is normal. Use a soft brush and avoid very hot or cold foods until it settles.
- Follow the home-care guidance you were given.

## Does insurance cover cleanings?

Most dental plans cover at least one preventive cleaning every six months. Many cover two per year in full; some provide partial coverage for more frequent visits. We accept most major PPO plans and can pre-verify your benefits and give you an estimate before treatment. [Contact us](/contact/) or call (661) 254-5200 to confirm your plan.

## When to come in sooner

- Persistent bleeding, swelling or new pain
- Bad breath that does not improve with brushing and flossing
- Loosening teeth, worsening sensitivity or trouble chewing
- After medical treatments such as chemotherapy that raise oral health risk

## Book your cleaning

Regular cleanings protect your smile and your budget. Call (661) 254-5200 to schedule a hygiene visit at our Valencia office. If it is your first time with us, read our [first visit guide](/why-choose-valencia-smile-what-to-expect-on-your-first-visit/) to know what to expect, or explore [dental crowns](/services/dental-crowns/) and [dental implants](/services/dental-implants/) if you are maintaining restorations.

faq.q: How often do I need a cleaning?
faq.a: Most adults with healthy gums do well every six months. If you have gum disease, implants or other risk factors, Dr. Lavi may recommend every two to four months. Your schedule is personalized during your exam.

faq.q: Will insurance cover a dental cleaning?
faq.a: Many dental plans cover preventive cleanings, often one or two per year. Coverage varies by policy. We can pre-verify your benefits and give you an estimate when you book.
